data.narrative:
Augury is a Series F robotics and manufacturing software company founded by Gal Shaul and Saar Yoskovitz, having raised $369M to date. The target operates within a 10-company peer universe in Robotics & Manufacturing, comprising 1 public comparable (277810.KQ) and 8 private peers including Locus Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach for this valuation. Using total capital raised ($369M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.3x step-up multiplier typical of Series F to subsequent-stage advancement yields an implied value of $480M. The peer-median method was not applicable given insufficient narrow-stage peers within the Robotics & Manufacturing cohort—while 10 same-sector companies exist, only one same-stage and one adjacent-stage peer were identified, falling short of the three-datapoint threshold needed for reliable median calculation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $408M (low) to $552M (high), with a median point estimate of $480M. This range reflects conservative application of stage-based progression mechanics. Key uncertainties center on the limited comparables in Augury's specific niche, customer concentration and revenue quality relative to peer cohorts, and technology differentiation in an increasingly crowded manufacturing robotics space. A robust next-stage valuation would require either tighter peer data at Series F or updated revenue and profitability metrics.
